## Motivation

Fixes #40155.

`Scheduler.run_batch` drives all speculative decoding through `BaseSpecWorker.forward_batch_generation`, and on the non-overlap path it passes `pp_proxy_tensors` unconditionally — whatever the pp size:

- `srt/managers/scheduler.py:4752` and `:4765` — `self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(batch, pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors)`

`FrozenKVMTPWorkerV2` and `UnoWorkerV2` never took the keyword, so any request routed through them dies on the first speculative step with:

```
TypeError: <Worker>.forward_batch_generation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'
```

Root cause: `BaseSpecWorker` is an ABC but never declared `forward_batch_generation`, so nothing enforced the interface the scheduler calls through. Each worker evolved its own signature and two of them silently fell behind.

This is a revival of a fix that has twice gone stale: #44211 (closed unmerged) and #42165 (open, inactive since 2026-10-02). Credit for the approach — accept-and-forward on frozen, discard on uno, abstract declaration on the base — belongs to their authors. #44490 is a parallel fix for the same issue; ours additionally adds the interface test the issue requested (part 2), and the two agree on the core changes.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/speculative/frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`**

Accept `pp_proxy_tensors=None` and forward it — to the target worker on the prefill branch (mirroring `EAGLEWorkerV2._forward_prefill_batch`), and to `self.verify()` on the decode branch (the inherited `EAGLEWorkerV2.verify` already takes it).

**`python/sglang/srt/speculative/uno_worker_v2.py`**

Accept `pp_proxy_tensors=None` and drop it. UNO is startup-gated to TP=PP=1 (`speculative_hook.py` `_handle_uno`), so the scheduler never hands it real proxy tensors; accepting the keyword keeps the shared call shape valid.

**`python/sglang/srt/speculative/base_spec_worker.py`**

Declare `forward_batch_generation` as an abstract method on `BaseSpecWorker`, so a worker that falls behind the interface fails at construction instead of mid-request. All existing workers already implement it, so nothing else changes.

**`test/registered/spec/test_spec_worker_interface.py`** (new)

Signature-inspection test that walks `sglang.srt.speculative` and asserts every worker that defines `forward_batch_generation` accepts both scheduler keywords (`on_publish`, `pp_proxy_tensors`). A new worker that drops them fails CI the day it lands, not in production.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — no kernel, model forward, or sampling change. Call binding only; greedy outputs are unaffected by construction.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — no execution-path change beyond accepting a keyword that is `None` on the affected configs (UNO: always, per the TP=PP=1 gate; frozen: forwarded to the existing target-worker parameter).

## Verification

- All 8 `forward_batch_generation` definitions in `sglang.srt.speculative` (eagle, dflash, dspark, ngram, multi_layer_eagle, frozen_kv_mtp, uno, base) accept both keywords — verified by AST signature check on the real sources.
- `BaseSpecWorker` ABC gate verified: a subclass missing the override raises `TypeError` at construction; a conforming subclass instantiates.
- Negative control: the same signature check against the pre-fix `origin/main` versions of both workers fails — the check detects exactly the bug this PR fixes.
- The registered test (`test/registered/spec/test_spec_worker_interface.py`) runs in CPU CI; it imports the full speculative package and walks it, so any worker that regresses the interface fails at collection.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidelines](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

(docs: no user-facing change to document; accuracy/speed benchmarks: not applicable for a call-binding fix, as stated above.)

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+"""Every spec worker must accept the keywords the scheduler passes it.
+
+``Scheduler.run_batch`` drives all speculative decoding through
+``BaseSpecWorker.forward_batch_generation``, and two of its keywords are
+unconditional: ``on_publish`` on the overlap path, and ``pp_proxy_tensors``
+on the non-overlap one, which passes it whatever the pp size. A worker that
+falls behind them raises ``TypeError`` on the first request down that path --
+not at import, not at construction -- which is how #39262 and #40155 were
+found. ``grammar_barrier`` is conditional on the algorithm, so it is left out
+here.
+
+Signature inspection only: no model, no device, no forward.
+
+    python -m pytest test/registered/spec/test_spec_worker_interface.py -v
+"""
+
+import importlib
+import inspect
+import pkgutil
+import unittest
+
+import sglang.srt.speculative as speculative
+from sglang.srt.speculative.base_spec_worker import BaseSpecWorker
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+# What Scheduler.run_batch hands every worker, regardless of algorithm.
+SCHEDULER_KEYWORDS = ("on_publish", "pp_proxy_tensors")
+
+
+def _workers_defining_the_call():
+    """Every BaseSpecWorker subclass that writes its own forward_batch_generation.
+
+    The package is walked rather than listed so a new worker is covered the
+    day it lands. Subclasses that inherit the call are covered through the
+    class that defines it.
+    """
+    for module in pkgutil.walk_packages(
+        speculative.__path__, speculative.__name__ + "."
+    ):
+        importlib.import_module(module.name)
+
+    workers = {}
+    pending = list(BaseSpecWorker.__subclasses__())
+    while pending:
+        worker = pending.pop()
+        pending.extend(worker.__subclasses__())
+        if "forward_batch_generation" in worker.__dict__:
+            workers[worker.__name__] = worker
+    return workers
+
+
+def _accepts_keyword(func, name: str) -> bool:
+    parameters = inspect.signature(func).parameters
+    if any(p.kind is p.VAR_KEYWORD for p in parameters.values()):
+        return True
+    parameter = parameters.get(name)
+    return parameter is not None and parameter.kind in (
+        inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
+        inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+    )
+
+
+class TestSpecWorkerForwardInterface(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_the_base_class_declares_the_call(self):
+        self.assertIn(
+            "forward_batch_generation",
+            BaseSpecWorker.__abstractmethods__,
+            "a worker missing the call the scheduler drives it through should "
+            "fail at construction, not mid-request",
+        )
+
+    def test_the_walk_finds_workers(self):
+        self.assertTrue(_workers_defining_the_call(), "no spec worker found to check")
+
+    def test_workers_accept_the_scheduler_keywords(self):
+        for name, worker in sorted(_workers_defining_the_call().items()):
+            for keyword in SCHEDULER_KEYWORDS:
+                with self.subTest(worker=name, keyword=keyword):
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        _accepts_keyword(worker.forward_batch_generation, keyword),
+                        f"{name}.forward_batch_generation drops {keyword}, which "
+                        "Scheduler.run_batch passes to every spec worker",
+                    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
